DALIO WARNS CHINA AND JAPAN COULD PULL BACK FROM TREASURIES Ray Dalio warns U.S. Treasuries are vulnerable to weakening demand from China and Japan, two of America’s largest foreign creditors. China’s holdings have fallen from $1.3 trillion in 2013 to about $618 billion, while Japan holds roughly $1.1 trillion. Dalio says reduced foreign demand could intensify pressure on U.S. borrowing as 10-year yields hover near 5.3%.

TSLA - GOLDMAN: TESLA’S AI STORY MATTERS MORE THAN Q3 EARNINGS Goldman Sachs reiterated its Neutral rating and $360 price target on Tesla ahead of Q3 earnings. The bank expects improving vehicle revenue from the Model Y L ramp, but says higher costs and capex could limit 2026 EPS upside. Goldman believes robotaxis, FSD and humanoid robots will matter more for Tesla’s stock reaction than Q3 earnings themselves.

JULIUS BAER SEES FINAL FED HIKE IN DECEMBER Julius Baer expects the Fed to deliver one final 25bp rate hike in December, followed by an extended pause. The bank points to a cooling U.S. labor market and sharply tighter financial conditions, driven more by rising long-term Treasury yields and a stronger dollar than by higher short-term rates. December is now seen as the most likely window for the final hike.

TRUMP SAYS U.S. WILL CONSIDER PERMANENT MILITARY BASE IN LITHUANIA President Trump says the U.S. will consider establishing a permanent military base in Lithuania, potentially replacing the current rotational model. Lithuania’s prime minister says the country is prepared to cover the costs of hosting a permanent U.S. presence. Around 1,000 U.S. troops have typically rotated through Lithuania, which has hosted American forces since 2014.

U.S. YIELDS RETREAT FROM 24-YEAR HIGHS Treasury yields pulled back as oil fell below $100 and Scott Bessent pledged that stronger growth and spending restraint would begin improving the U.S. debt trajectory. The 10-year yield fell to 5.27% and the 30-year to 5.63%, easing from levels last seen in 2002. Investors remain cautious, however, with the U.S. deficit near 6% of GDP and markets still pricing substantial Fed tightening.

But Hardy warns inventory buffers in the West are largely gone, and without these flows oil could face a $200-per-barrel scenario. S&P 500 ON TRACK FOR 28TH RECORD CLOSE OF 2026 The S&P 500 rose nearly 0.5% to around 7,810, putting it on course to surpass its Aug. 13 record closing high. The index is also approaching its 7,816.70 intraday record. A new high would mark the S&P 500’s 28th record close this year, while the Nasdaq is on track for a second consecutive record close.

U.S. GASOLINE AND DIESEL PRICES EASE, BUT REMAIN SHARPLY HIGHER U.S. regular gasoline fell slightly to $4.354 per gallon, but remains $1.23 higher than a year ago. Diesel saw a much larger weekly decline, falling 18.3 cents to $6.199 per gallon, yet remains $2.49 above year-ago levels. The Lower Atlantic recorded the largest declines, with gasoline falling 23.6 cents and diesel dropping 25.4 cents.

YELLEN BACKS RETALIATION AGAINST TRUMP TARIFFS Former Treasury Secretary Janet Yellen called President Trump’s treatment of U.S. allies “appalling” and said Canada and other countries should retaliate against protectionist measures rather than “accept this lying down.” Yellen argues tariffs have worsened affordability for Americans, while weakening cooperation with allies. Bloomberg Economics estimates the U.S. effective tariff rate at 11.2%, nearly 9 percentage points above early 2025 levels.

TRUMP DIESEL TAX RELIEF CALLED A “BAND AID” U.S. diesel futures fell after President Trump temporarily allowed tax-deferred on-road use of red diesel through year-end, with the deferred federal excise tax potentially eliminated later. Ritterbusch says the measure may provide some relief but doesn’t address the underlying supply disruption through the Strait of Hormuz. Nymex diesel fell 2.6% to $4.4295 per gallon.

DRONE ATTACK SHUTS MAJOR RUSSIAN OIL REFINERY Russia’s Volgograd refinery completely halted crude processing on October 2 after equipment was damaged in a drone attack, industry sources told Reuters. The Lukoil-owned facility can process around 280,000 barrels per day, representing roughly 5% of Russia’s total refining capacity. The shutdown threatens to intensify Russia’s existing fuel crunch, as repeated attacks increasingly disrupt the country’s refining infrastructure.

BOJ’S SATO BACKS FURTHER RATE HIKES, BUT FLAGS WEAK CONSUMPTION BOJ board member Ayano Sato supports gradually raising interest rates, saying tighter policy can contribute to sustainable economic growth, but declined to specify the timing of the next hike. Sato, who opposed a rate hike at September’s meeting, said the decision reflected concern that consumer spending lacked momentum. DIMON WARNS AI HAS INCREASED CYBER RISK TENFOLD JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon says AI has increased cyber risk tenfold, making cybersecurity the bank’s biggest threat. He also warned governments “can’t borrow endlessly and spend endlessly,” as rising debt could push yields and credit spreads higher. On AI infrastructure, Dimon said companies should build data centers where communities want them, while arguing better policy could boost growth without additional spending.

EXPLOSION HEARD NEAR IRAN’S QESHM ISLAND The sound of an explosion was heard from the direction of the sea near Iran’s Qeshm Island, according to IRNA. No impact or strike has been reported on the island itself, and local sources have not yet provided further details. The cause of the explosion remains unclear.

U.S. POWER DEMAND TO HIT RECORD HIGHS ON AI BOOM U.S. electricity consumption is projected to reach record highs in both 2026 and 2027, driven partly by growing demand from AI and crypto data centers, according to the EIA. Power demand is expected to rise from 4,195 billion kWh in 2025 to 4,356 billion kWh in 2027. Renewables’ generation share is projected to reach 27% by 2027, while coal falls to 15%.

U.S. PRESSES RUSSIA FOR ANSWERS OVER SIBERIA LAB DEATH The U.S. has formally pressed Russia for more information after a worker at a Siberian plague research center died from an unexplained pneumonia, according to the WSJ. Secretary of State Marco Rubio said Moscow has provided “still quite limited” information, while Russia says testing found no pathogen linked to her work. The WHO currently assesses the international health risk as “very low.”

FRANCE READY TO BYPASS PARLIAMENT FOR €43 BILLION IN CUTS French Finance Minister Roland Lescure says the government is prepared to use constitutional powers to pass its 2027 budget without a parliamentary vote if negotiations fail. The plan includes roughly €43 billion in spending cuts, with Lescure insisting the deficit must not exceed 5% of GDP. Invoking Article 49.3 could trigger a no-confidence vote, raising political risk as French borrowing costs remain under pressure.

BNP WARNS AXING 20-YEAR TREASURY COULD BACKFIRE BNP Paribas warns eliminating the 20-year Treasury bond could push yields higher, signaling panic and encouraging bond vigilantes rather than lowering borrowing costs. The bank maintains its 30-year Treasury short, targeting a yield of 5.8% versus 5.64% currently. BNP says Treasury interventions are ultimately a “band-aid on a gunshot wound” unless underlying inflation and fiscal deficits are addressed.

U.S. 30-YEAR YIELD HITS NEW 24-YEAR HIGH The 30-year Treasury yield climbed to 5.706%, its highest since 2002, as the global bond selloff resumed ahead of Fed minutes. The 10-year yield rose to 5.323%, while Brent crude topped $101 amid renewed geopolitical pressure. Danske Bank warns both 10- and 30-year Treasury yields could reach 6% as investors demand higher long-term risk premiums.

U.S. 10-YEAR TREASURY AUCTION DRAWS STRONG DEMAND The Treasury sold $39 billion of 9-year 10-month notes at a 5.300% high yield, with a 2.77 bid-to-cover ratio. Indirect bidders took a strong 80.34%, direct bidders 17.12%, while primary dealers were left with just 2.54% — signaling solid end-investor demand.

SMALL MORTGAGES ARE DISAPPEARING ACROSS THE U.S. Mortgages of $100,000 or less accounted for less than 3% of U.S. home loans in 2025-26, down from more than 12% in 2013-14, according to Realtor The decline reflects fewer low-priced homes and persistent barriers to issuing smaller loans, limiting financing options for lower-cost buyers. The median 2026 purchase price for homes financed with small mortgages was $109,681.

TRUMP TO UNVEIL $1 BILLION+ AI SCIENCE PUSH President Trump will attend a White House summit Thursday focused on using advanced AI to accelerate scientific breakthroughs and strengthen U.S. leadership. The administration will announce more than $1 billion in industry commitments to its Genesis Mission from OpenAI, Anthropic, AMD and others. Federal agencies will also invest over $100 million in AI-driven science tools, alongside a new 14-institution compute hub spanning 10 southeastern states.
